title: Mode (predicating-regime fiber restriction; ω < κ < ω₁)
description: Regime: transfinite-predication-category (predicating morphism, ω < κ < ω₁). Per lab/.../predicated-agentic-orchestration-platform/mode/mode.md: 'A further restriction within an agent's active view: a substrate-recorded constraint that narrows what the agent can do during a particular interaction phase, beyond what the agent's general authorization admits... A mode is recorded as predications on the view (or on the agent's session entity), declaring which authorization positions are active during the mode.' Mode is a fiber restriction (predicating regime act) — it refines a predication-cell on the agent's authorization view, narrowing which operations the substrate's closure rules will admit during the interaction phase. Three engineering properties from the lab source: (1) modes are substrate entities, queryable through the same operators as the rest of the substrate; (2) mode transitions are events producing witness entries; (3) mode is constraint — a structural narrowing of authorization — not declaration.
